page: Microsoft Azure E8ns_v6 is an Env6-family virtual machine configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB memory-to-core ratio. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz, this x86_64 architecture server features 4 physical cores with hyper-threading. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for tile and INT8 operations. The instance operates on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, lacks local storage, and contains no GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations place the E8ns_v6 in the average performance tier across most categories. It achieves a single-core stress-ng CPU score of 1917.38 and a multi-core score of 7845.77. Memory bandwidth tests show 608.18 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 61.47 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads, and 42.33 GB/sec for large-block writes. The system demonstrates strong text generation performance on small language models at 311.01 tokens per second, though text generation on medium models drops to a weaker 8.17 tokens per second. Database operations score 4759.95 on PassMark, and Redis SET operations reach 10.8 million operations per second.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and lack of local storage, the E8ns_v6 offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that rely on external Premium Storage. The absence of local NVMe drives means storage costs are decoupled from compute, allowing optimization for workloads that do not require high-speed local scratch space. This server is suited for memory-optimized tasks, database operations, caching layers like Redis, and lightweight language model inference where high memory capacity per core is required without the need for dedicated GPU acceleration.
